title: Interactive admin sign-in (code + PKCE)
lede: An administrator signs in through PingOne's authorization server; the tokens stay on this app's server. Simulated in Mock.

nodes.label: Your browser
sub: This page. Never sees a token.

nodes.label: This app (server)
sub: Holds secrets and tokens, runs the safety gate, writes the audit.

steps.title: You press Sign in
steps.what: You press Sign in. This app prepares a state, a nonce and a PKCE challenge and answers with the authorization URL.

steps.title: Your browser goes to PingOne
steps.what: Your browser goes to PingOne's authorization server. This is the tool's connection to a third party, not a sign-in to this app.

steps.title: PingOne sends the code back
steps.what: PingOne redirects back to the exact registered loopback address with a one-time code and the state.

steps.title: This app exchanges the code
steps.what: This app checks the state, exchanges the code with the PKCE verifier, and validates the issuer and nonce.

steps.title: Tokens stay on the server
steps.what: Access and refresh tokens are kept on the server. The page shows only who is signed in.

steps.title: Calls carry the admin's own token
steps.what: Calls go to the hosted MCP server with the admin's own token, so the list matches that admin's roles.

steps.title: The server acts as that admin
steps.what: The server acts on the admin plane with that admin's permissions.
